tier_reason: BENCHMARKS.md is a first-party two-machine comparison against tokio, with a named rig, Little's-law validity gates and reproduction commands. The echo harness is public (ringline-bench/src/bin/server.rs has the --tokio-scheduler/--echo-mode arms), but the echo CPU is only 'Xeon' and neither run gives a rustc version or build flags. The segcache harness is said to live on branch bench/fair-throughput, which no longer exists, so this is not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: TCP echo (Sept 2026, commit a685e16): against the best of five tokio configurations, ringline leads in 13 of 16 cells, from -10.3% to +8.9% (the page says 'roughly 0-10% faster'). It loses at 16 KiB/64 conns (-10.3%), 16 KiB/512 (-4.9%) and 4 KiB/64 (-0.1%). Against tokio's default multi-thread runtime it is +4% to +71% (256 B: +4/+70/+46/+27%; 4 KiB: +16/+57/+36/+33%; 16 KiB: +42/+71/+51%). The page itself retracts the earlier '27-71%' lead because it implied a win over tokio's best configuration. At 512 conns/256 B it does 619,863 ops/s against 591,854 for tokio-uring and 425,486 for default tokio. Segcache GET (June 2026, v0.1.3, 4 workers, 128 conns): at 256 B/1 KiB, +31%/+30% throughput, -28%/-24% p50, -15%/-18% p99, +22%/+23% ops/core-s. At 4 KiB, throughput and p50 tie, p99 is -8% and ops/core-s +14%. At open-loop saturation the two tie (NIC/PPS-bound).
corrections.hardware: Echo run: server is a 24 vCPU Xeon (hv02 guest), client a 56 vCPU Xeon (hv01 guest). The page says 'bare metal', but the runs were SystemsLab anvil-vm jobs with the X710 PFs passed through. Network is 4x Intel X710 in a direct-attached 40G LAG; no CPU model is given. 8 server workers, 16 client threads. Segcache run: AWS c8g.4xlarge (16 vCPU Graviton4, Neoverse-V2) server and c8g.8xlarge (32 vCPU Graviton4) client, same AZ, cluster placement group, Debian 13, Linux 6.12.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Rust 'stable' (segcache run only). Neither run gives a rustc version or build flags. The workspace has edition 2024 and MSRV 1.88, no [profile.release] overrides and no rust-toolchain pin.
corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark in the project's own repo, not independent. It stays below Tier A because the echo CPU is only 'Xeon', no rustc version or build flags are given, and the segcache harness is said to be on branch bench/fair-throughput, which no longer exists on GitHub; only the echo harness (ringline-bench) is on main. The retraction of the earlier 27-71% headline is in BENCHMARKS.md's own 'Read this first' section, not in the README. The README's Benchmarks section still describes only the June 2026 segcache run. Segcache is the only protocol-like workload. It is stale (ringline 0.1.3, June 2026), predates the harness fairness fix #392, compares against a single tokio configuration, and ties at open-loop saturation. The echo run is a byte pipe with no parsing, and its 2048-connection column is labelled directional. ringline loses to splice-based tokio at 16 KiB. The echo rig is called bare metal but was run as VM guests with NIC passthrough. The README says ringline is not a tokio replacement and is not API-compatible.

notes: The page's numbers match the record. The segcache figures are exact. I rewrote claimed_speedup because the default-tokio range is really +4% to +71% (the 1-connection cells are +4%/+16%), and the 'best tokio' comparison includes losses of up to 10.3%. I also fixed the caveat that credited the retraction to the README (it is in BENCHMARKS.md). The license is dual MIT OR Apache-2.0 (Cargo.toml, README, and both LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE files), even though GitHub's API reports only Apache-2.0. The last commit is 2026-09-26; the repo is not archived and not a fork.
